title: A toilet is not a trash can.
accent: That is how a 130-tonne blockage in London started.

title: 130 tonnes, 250 metres
body: A “fatberg” found in the sewer under Whitechapel Road.
Wet wipes, nappies, fat and oil, all set hard like concrete.
It weighed as much as 11 double-decker buses. Crews spent 3 weeks breaking it up.

title: Wet wipes
body: When UK sewer blockages were examined, 93% of the material was wet wipes.
The UK has ~300,000 blockages a year, costing £100 million to clear.
Toilet paper made up less than 1%.

title: Don't trust the pack
body: In Canada, 101 different wipes were tested. 23 were labelled “flushable”.
Not one broke down enough in water.
Most contain synthetic fibres, in other words plastic.

title: Hot water won't save the grease
body: Pour pan grease down the sink with hot water and it cools and hardens further down the pipe.
Dish soap doesn't help either. The grease still sets later.
A little each time, and over the years the pipe keeps narrowing.

title: Protect your pipes
steps: Only toilet paper goes in the toilet
Wipes, cotton, nappies: in the bin
Collect cooled grease in a lidded jar
Wipe the pan with paper before washing
note: Easiest fix: keep a small bin next to the toilet.

title: What else do you want to know about water?
accent: Tell me in the comments. The next post will be about it.
